title: Which Parfums de Marly Should You Try First? Layton, Pegasus, Althair, Perseus and Haltane Compared
summary: A decision guide to five Parfums de Marly fragrances that sends you from a smell you already like to the one to try first, using only the notes on each maker page. It also compares three pairs by their official notes and explains where the house name comes from.
tags: which parfums de marly to try first
author: Jeff Theefs
image_alt: Five generic unbranded clear-glass 5 ml atomizers with plain silver caps in a loose row on a cream travertine surface beside folded linen, a small brass dish and a plain brown leather glove in soft morning light
seo_title: Which Parfums de Marly to Try First? 5 Compared | Base Note
seo_description: Pick your first Parfums de Marly by a note you already like: apple and lavender, vanilla and cinnamon, grapefruit, almond or leather. Official notes compared.

fig-01.alt: Three step picture: pick a smell you already like, such as apple; find that smell in the note lists; try that fragrance first.
fig-01.caption: Start from a smell you already enjoy, then find it in each fragrance's note list.

fig-02.alt: Decision chart that starts from a smell you already like and routes to one of five Parfums de Marly fragrances: apple and lavender to Layton, cinnamon and orange blossom to Althair, praline and leather to Haltane, grapefruit and vetiver to Perseus, almond and anise to Pegasus
fig-02.caption: Built only from each official note list. The order follows shared notes and is not a quality ranking.

fig-03.alt: Ingredient still life on cream travertine with a forest-green linen runner: an apple, lavender sprigs, vanilla pods, half a pink grapefruit, whole almonds, cinnamon sticks and green cardamom pods

fig-04.alt: Seven generic unbranded clear-glass 5 ml atomizers on an oak dressing table, five standing and two resting in a forest-green ceramic dish, beside a plain brown leather watch strap, a small brass tray and folded cream linen
